title: A T3 Code message that pairs in time for its own lead but too late to vouch for the reading before it

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: M1's 135 characters type in 135 / 1.5 = 90 s, from 19:00:00 to its stamp at 19:01:30. It is the thread's first message, so no earlier one caps the lead.

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: T3 hands M1 to the agent at 19:01:31, so 19:01:30 is in neither the lead nor a turn. T1 runs from 19:01:31.

rows.sm: 2.4: no relayed session reads while its agent runs
2.4: a message that pairs more than PENDING_WINDOW_S - 60 s after a stop vouches for no reading of it
rows.note: T1 stops at 19:06:00 with 20 + 20 + 60 + 20 = 120 s in its bucket, the cap. M2, the thread's next relayed message, is sent 590 s after the stop, but its prompt comes at 19:25:41, so it pairs 1,181 s after the stop, past 840 s, and vouches for no reading of it. Without that deadline the session would read 19:06:00 to 19:08:00 here, READ 60 in each minute, though both minutes are final, at 19:22:00 and 19:23:00, before M2 pairs. No credit and no agent running.

rows.sm: 5.1: no credit and no agent running
rows.note: Even without the deadline the bucket would be empty from 19:08:00, and the reading would end at 19:10:00, when A1 starts.

rows.sm: 2.2 rule 4: no relay record, so the agent's message is headless
rows.note: An agent in the docs thread sends this thread a message through T3's MCP tools. T3 stores it with createdBy agent, so the reader writes no record, nothing witnesses its prompt at 19:10:00, and rule 4 makes it headless: A1 runs, automated, from 19:10:00.

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: M2's 105 characters type in 105 / 1.5 = 70 s, from 19:14:40 to its stamp at 19:15:50, under A1's run. M1 was sent 860 s before M2, so the cap at the seconds since the thread's previous message doesn't bind.

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: M2 is sent at 19:15:50, and T3 queues it behind A1. The reader records it at 19:15:53, before any prompt, so the record names none. The lead's minutes wait for the pairing, and they stay pending until 19:30:00 and 19:31:00.

A1 stops at 19:25:40, and T3 hands M2's run to the agent at 19:25:41, 591 s after M2's stamp, inside RELAY_MATCH_S. The prompt names M2's record, so M2 pairs and its lead stands. 19:25:40 is between the turns. T2 runs from 19:25:41, and its prompt resets the bucket to its 20 s base.

2.4: a relayed session reads after a stop, until the thread's next relayed message, sent within 600 s and paired within 840 s of the stop
rows.note: T2 stops at 19:34:00 with 20 + 20 + 45 + 35 = 120 s in its bucket. M3 is sent at 19:37:00, 180 s after the stop, and pairs at 19:37:03, 183 s after it, so the session reads from the stop.

rows.note: The 120 s end at 19:36:00. T2 filled the cap exactly, so no second is X.bucket_cap.

rows.note: M3's 90 characters type in 90 / 1.5 = 60 s, from 19:36:00 to its stamp at 19:37:00. M2 was sent 1,270 s earlier.
T3 hands M3 over at 19:37:01, and the reader records it at 19:37:03, naming the prompt. M3's turn runs from 19:37:01.

notes: No SM section describes this case. Every row comes from SM 2.2 rules 4 and 9, 2.3, 2.4 and 5.2 as docs/errata/2026-11-22-relayed-prompts.md applies them, with 2.4's deadline for the pairing that vouches for a stop's reading: PENDING_WINDOW_S - 60 s = 840 s after the stop. Every credited second is level C with via_relay, and witnessed: the server uploads live.

The server has no desktop, so pairtime samples no presence and records no focus: every slot's presence is unknown, and uncredited seconds take SM 5.2's codes for such a slot. No second is X.bucket_cap: the one reading drains a bucket T2 filled to exactly the 120 s cap.

The agent's message comes from a T3 thread on a provider pairtime has no hooks for, so this device records nothing of the agent that sent it. T3 stores the message with createdBy agent, so the T3 reader writes no record for it.

Without the 840 s deadline, M2, sent 590 s after T1's stop, would vouch for T1's reading: READ 60 in 19:06 and 60 in 19:07, and 460 s in all. Both minutes are final, at 19:22:00 and 19:23:00, before M2 pairs at 19:25:41.
relayed_prompts counts the prompts a relay record witnessed; headless_prompts the agent's message, which rule 4 took.
